text:
Sam: Heads-up — KV cache steady memory growth on INT8 longctx runs. Not a short spike; looks linear over ~12h. Posting profiler snippet.

Anya: can you drop the profiler output + exact run args?

Sam: Pasted below (short). model: rwlm-13b-ctx16k-int8, seq=8192 avg, batch_tokens=5200, quant=dynamic-8.
```
step   kv_mem_mb   slot_frag_pct   resident_slots   avg_slot_size_kb
0      1280        22              51200            25
1000   1456        34              57600            26
10000  1936        66              70400            27
24h    2128        71              73600            28

observations: eviction_count very low, page_reuse drops after warmup, singleflight_coalesce shows high contention.
```

Devon: did we ship a kernel-selection tweak recently for INT8 inference? commit?

Sam: No kernel changes since 2 weeks ago (link: https://git/revs/abc123). This looks like a control-plane heuristic + cache lifecycle mismatch for quantized slots.

Maria: What's the accuracy delta when you run INT8 vs BF16? quick numbers please.

Sam: quick eval on our safety/llm-eval set: BF16 baseline -> perplexity 12.3; INT8 -> 13.8 (+12%). Memory: INT8 reduced KV mem ~42% vs BF16 across steady-state.

Lucas: That tradeoff is big. Could be that INT8 compaction changes slot bitmaps and increases fragmentation; small slots don't coalesce well. Try forcing slab-coalesce on write and bump eviction_hysteresis from 50ms -> 250ms.

Anya: also check batching heuristics — if batch tokens jump, the KV residency profile changes (more hot prefixes). Could mask as leak.

Sam: Re-ran a short A/B with eviction_hysteresis=250ms + slab_coalesce=on. Results (6h):
```
kv_mem_mb: 2100 -> 1580 (stable), slot_frag: 71% -> 39%, evict_ops up 3x (expected), avg_latency p95 +2ms.
accuracy: INT8 still +11% perplexity vs BF16.
```

Devon: Interesting. So enabling coalescing trades latency for mem. We should confirm kernel path isn't causing unexpected rounding in KV index math for quantized pages.

InfraBot: ci-bench: kv-longctx-int8-evict-250ms completed — artifacts at https://ci/artifacts/2666.

Maria: For product decision we need a full 24h run on realistic traffic plus the eval suite. Sam, can you queue that and include a BF16 baseline?

Sam: Queued 24h + BF16 baseline. command I used: 
```bash
./run_bench --model rwlm-13b --ctx 16384 --quant int8 --batch_tokens 5200 --evict_hysteresis_ms 250 --slab_coalesce on --tag kv-int8-hyst250-2026-03
```

Lucas: Also add a run with dynamic singleflight disabled (set singleflight_coalesce=false) — I suspect coalescing is keeping more partial prefixes pinned.

Anya: Good call. Add an eval job to compute embed/answer-bleu and log token-level mismatch.

Devon: I'll grep kernel dispatch logs for any fallback paths during the run. If the runtime selects an FP fallback for some blocks unexpectedly we might get inconsistent slot shapes.

Sam: ACTIONS:
- Sam: run the 24h INT8 (hysteresis=250, slab_coalesce=on) + INT8 singleflight=false variant + BF16 baseline.
- Maria: run eval suite and report perplexity + topk-token-diff.
- Devon: audit kernel-selection logs for any on-the-fly fallback or mixed-exec patterns.
- Lucas: prepare a short doc on slab-coalesce latency/memory tradeoffs for eng-runtime digest.

Sam: I'll post results tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
